Welcome

Welcome to the National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy

Welcome to the National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy, India's premier gathering dedicated to advancing Homoeopathy under the theme “Homoeopathy in Contemporary Healthcare: Evidence, Innovation, Research and Integrative Approaches for Emerging Health Challenges.”

National Scientific Convention · 2026

National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy 2026

The National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy 2026 will be held at Dr. Abhin Chandra Homoeopathic Medical College & Hospital, Bhubaneswar, Odisha, from 24 November 2026.

Organised by Dr. Abhin Chandra Homoeopathic Medical College & Hospital, with active participation from CCRH, NCH, the Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India, and the Health and Family Welfare Department, Government of Odisha, this prestigious gathering will bring together thought leaders, practitioners and researchers from across India.

Our Institution

ABOUT THE INSTITUTION

Dr. Abhin Chandra Homoeopathic Medical College and Hospital, Bhubaneswar is a premier Homoeopathic Medical College of Odisha and one of the pioneer institutions of the country. It is the first Government Homoeopathic Medical College & Hospital of the country, established in 1969 with active support from the Ministry of Health, Odisha, and became functional in the same year. Initially, the college was named Government Homoeopathic Medical College & Hospital; subsequently, it was renamed Dr. Abhin Chandra Homoeopathic Medical College and Hospital. The college was named after Late Padmashree Dr. Abhin Chandra Rao, the legendary Homoeopathic physician who served as Honorary Physician to three former Presidents of India.

The college is located in the central capital region beside Janpath Road, Bhubaneswar, on approximately 8 acres of land, a few furlongs from the Railway Station and a few miles from Biju Patnaik International Airport. The college has a 50-bedded hospital with 19 different outpatient departments and a 24×7 casualty department, providing healthcare delivery through a holistic Homoeopathic approach. Adequate provisions have been made for teaching and accommodation for admitted students. The campus also has a well-maintained 2-acre herbal garden with uncommon and valuable varieties of medicinal plants for teaching and research.

The college has 12 well-equipped teaching departments and a magnificent library containing books of rare collections. Following its establishment, the DHMS (Diploma in Homoeopathic Medicines and Surgery) course continued from 1969–1970 to 1976–1977. Subsequently, in 1977–1978, the BHMS (Bachelor of Homoeopathic Medicine and Surgery) course was introduced, affiliated with Utkal University, Vani Vihar, Bhubaneswar, and has continued since then.

Admissions to UG and PG courses are granted under the framework of the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH), Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India. The admission process is conducted through NEET and AIAPGET examinations, with counselling through AACCC and OJEE, Odisha.
